statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 3% (low), with no Nasdaq-100 price path available during the CME weekend halt.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON. A narrow danger window is published across the 22:00Z CME reopen (00:00 Berlin on 5 October), where the forecast Tail path reaches the WATCH band on gap and discontinuity risk.
headline: Nasdaq-100 at a record close into the weekend futures halt, with an intensifying but unconfirmed Saudi escalation framing the Sunday reopen
body: CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists to assess and Tail stays at its structural floor. The last observed path was orderly: the index traded to an all-time intraday high of 31,017.53 on Friday 2 October, fully retraced it, and finished at a record 30,807.93 close in the lower quarter of the session range, up 1.00%, with VIX settling at 15.31, down 6.59%. That full retracement is two-way behaviour rather than the shallow-pullback structure Tail measures. Stress is high rather than low because the macro backdrop behind that record close is unusually tense. Brent settled near 102.25 and WTI near 91.11, H.15 shows the 10-year near 5.24% and the 30-year near 5.61%, and the Saudi-Houthi conflict escalated further over the weekend. The Houthis claimed a ballistic-missile and drone strike on an Aramco facility south of Riyadh on 3 October, which the Saudi-led coalition spokesman called misleading; early on 4 October the coalition reported 97 targeting operations against Houthi forces on the Tor al-Baha front and the Taiz axis, and Reuters has reported that Riyadh is weighing a broader multi-front offensive to secure Red Sea shipping. Neither Saudi authorities nor Aramco have confirmed damage or any impact on production, refining or exports, and the G7 commitment to release up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel remains an active offsetting supply response. Event importance of this kind informs Stress and Confidence; it does not by itself establish the persistent no-retracement path that Tail measures. The Saudi Exchange trades on Sundays from 07:00Z to 12:00Z and provides the only live equity read before the CME reopen, but it is regional and cannot establish Nasdaq-100 structure. The published forecast therefore holds Tail at the floor through the closed session and raises it into the WATCH band only across the reopen hours, where gap and discontinuity risk is genuine but not yet observable.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 hours Claude published Tail between 8% and 3%, reaching a 3% floor from 12:00Z on 3 October and holding there, while Stress fell to 52% in the European afternoon and then rebuilt steadily to 73-75% through the weekend halt. Confidence stayed in the 83-88% band. Every hour mapped to EA_ON and green, and the dominant mode was normal throughout.
outlookSummary: The closed Sunday session carries no scoreable Nasdaq-100 structure, so Tail is held at 3-5% through 21:00Z while Stress rebuilds from 76% to a 79% peak as unpriced weekend headline flow accumulates. The Saudi Exchange session from 07:00Z to 12:00Z supplies the only live equity evidence before the reopen. Tail is raised to 21-23%, inside the WATCH band, for the 22:00Z CME reopen and the two hours after it, which form the published danger window. It then decays conditionally to 11% by 05:00Z on the assumption that price discovery is orderly, an assumption that NQ holding a session extreme without meaningful retracement would invalidate. Confidence troughs at 79% in the final closed hour and recovers to 85% once a continuous path is observable again.
